examples.purpose: Choosing how to pay, the guide's In context, with the sheet shown: the payment screen (a line of Text and its Change payment method Button) is dimmed by a bare Overlay, and the sheet titled “Pay with” docks to the bottom over it, holding the three payment options as List Items in a ListGroup. visible stands for the screen's shown state, which the Button's onPress sets; a row's onPress stands for keeping that choice and hiding the sheet, and the Overlay's onPress for hiding it on a tap on the dimmed screen. The screen renders the Overlay only while the sheet shows.
examples.jsx:
<Screen>
  <Text>Pay ₹500 to Asha Stores</Text>
  <Button label="Change payment method" onPress={() => {}} />
  <Overlay onPress={() => {}} />
  <ContentSheet visible title="Pay with">
    <ListGroup>
      <ListItem layout="Horizontal" title="UPI" supportText="Jio Payments Bank •• 4821" onPress={() => {}} />
      <ListItem layout="Horizontal" title="Debit card" supportText="•• 9012" onPress={() => {}} />
      <ListItem layout="Horizontal" title="Net banking" supportText="Any bank" onPress={() => {}} />
    </ListGroup>
  </ContentSheet>
</Screen>

Every guide and evidence sentence quoted here was read against the installed source (read, not rendered; token values through the package's own getVariableByName in lib/commonjs, Light): the defaults visible, pinToBottom and safeAreaBottom true, maxHeightPercent 0.7 (ContentSheet.tsx 228–240); the sheet is contentSheet/bg rgb(255, 255, 255) under MainPage and SubPage and rgb(245, 245, 245) under JioPlus, 8 px side padding, 12 px top, 41 px bottom plus the safe-area inset when safeAreaBottom is on (0 with no SafeAreaProvider, 244–254), top radius 20 and bottom radius 0, no handle (144–205); pinned, a host fills the parent (absolute, 0 on every side, 320–329, 417–424) and the sheet sits in it absolute at left, right and bottom 0 (207–212), so it docks to the bottom of its nearest positioned parent at full width (react-native-web Views are position relative); the title is a Text with accessibilityRole header (an h1 on the web, react-native-web's role mapping) in a header View outside the ScrollView, centred, 14/17 weight 700 rgb(13, 13, 15), with drawer/titleWrap padding 16 above and 8 below, so the header is 41 px and the slot starts 12 + 41 + 8 = 61 px from the top (291–295, 401–411); contentSheet/gap 8 separates the header from the scroller and the slot's children (401, 405); the maximum height is the measured parent height × maxHeightPercent, and the scroller's own maximum takes off the padding, the header and the gap, so past it only the slot scrolls, with the scrollbar hidden (270–300, 403–409); visible springs translateY between 0 and the window's height with the Drawer's spring (damping 32, stiffness 300; 60–67, 286–289), starting off-screen on mount; hidden, the sheet keeps its children mounted with accessibilityElementsHidden, importantForAccessibility no-hide-descendants and pointerEvents none, on the web aria-hidden, inert and tabIndex −1, and every focusable descendant at tabindex −1 (restored when shown; 357–397); there is no role, label, Escape or focus move on the sheet, and no close callback (the props). Overlay.tsx (dbe0e02): without trapFocus the focus trap does nothing (useWebFocusTrap returns at once when inactive, web-focus-trap.ts 109), the root is a plain View with no dialog role, and the scrim Pressable is tabIndex −1 and aria-hidden on the web (Overlay.tsx 102–160), so “leaves keyboard focus on the page” holds. No sentence quoted here is contradicted. Sizing's “8 px between the title and the content” is the gap between the 41 px header (Figma's 344 × 41 title wrap) and the slot, as the evidence measures it; the title's text sits 16 px above the content (the wrap's 8 px plus the gap). Its item 7 (the generated Storybook docs page) is not a Coin defect. #281 (Component Fix, Done, live 23 October, c8526ae) is fixed, and Overlay.tsx is the same on dbe0e02. Dark mode is not recorded (Dark set through modes gives a white title on an rgb(13, 13, 15) sheet, readableSheetBackground, 44–55; ContentSheet reads only its modes prop, not JFSThemeProvider, so Dark set only on the provider leaves the sheet and title light, as the evidence says). Not quoted: the evidence's Upstream mdx line (the 6 October generated page): upstream ContentSheet.mdx at dbe0e02 (76592ce, the same since c1fa197) is the handwritten rewrite and no longer has “Keep `safeAreaBottom` enabled”, “When used as a modal surface, manage focus and provide a dismiss affordance in the content” or “Do not set a fixed height” in those words; it names Drawer, ModalSheet and ActionFooter as the alternatives, but no guide or evidence sentence does, so avoidWhen has no useInstead. That mdx also says “The title is a Text node, not a header role”, which the source contradicts (accessibilityRole header); reported to the coordinator as a package docs note. Also left out: the Sources' Figma sentence (one 360 × 350 component; the package grows with its content, which the entry says), the evidence's Package line (6 October) and Storybook line (the published Storybook's age; its index on 31 October lists the four stories the Sources note names, and the docs page is an attached MDX whose version was not determined), the site's Reanimated stand-in and the docs-only #281 measurements. Strength: one quote holds an absolute word, /placementAdvice/3 “It never sets a height” (everywhere: the component itself sets no height in any use; behaviour, so recommended). Nothing is required: ContentSheet has no required prop and the guide no everywhere-absolute instruction. Anatomy required: Sheet and Slot are always drawn; Title only with a non-empty title. Cross-check round 1 flagged /useWhen/1 (the core principle, which describes behaviour, not a situation); it moved to /configuration/0. Round 2 raised none. Configuration from facts: visible, pinToBottom and safeAreaBottom say only what their type docs say. Not recorded as rules: maxHeightPercent (its fact and the evidence fact carry it; the guide's 70% is the default), avoidKeyboard and keyboardSpacing (deprecated, no effect), style (only the guide's fixed-height Don't; the building rules forbid colour, border, radius and font overrides), testID and the inherited View props; the modes Color Mode (building rules) and Page type (the guide shows none; kept as an evidence fact), and List Item Style Boxed, which the guide sets on every sheet's rows and ListGroup (its SHEET modes), a look no guide sentence asks for, so the examples' rows are default List Items. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode and no other modes (the guide sets Color Mode Light on everything); the guide's ScreenFrame is written as Screen, which has an undocumented entry; the In context screen is a Text, its Change payment method Button, a bare Overlay with onPress (rendered only while the sheet shows, as the guide does) and the sheet titled “Pay with” with the guide's three payment rows as Horizontal List Items in a ListGroup; the second example is that screen with the sheet hidden and no Overlay, as the In context screen is after a choice, matching the States' Hidden card (which uses the transaction rows). The transaction sheets (Configuration, States, Sizing, Do & Don'ts) are left out of examples: their rows show each amount with MoneyValue, which has no entry in this pack. Also left out: the anatomy and sizing specimens (pinToBottom false), the Do & Don'ts previews and the playground. Consistency with related entries: Overlay's entry agrees: its bare-scrim rule (“Leave the overlay empty (no children) when a sheet or drawer draws its own surface”), its required “Leave trapFocus off … for a scrim drawn under another surface”, its bare-scrim example and “Without trapFocus … the overlay leaves focus alone” are how this guide and its examples use Overlay. ModalSheet's entry agrees (“A new flow: it deserves its own screen; keep a sheet to one task” matches this guide's Content); unlike Content Sheet it has its own scrim, close and focus handling, which this entry's “no role, scrim, or close control of its own” keeps apart. Drawer's entry agrees (a Drawer has a handle and never closes; this sheet has no handle and the screen shows and hides it; both use the drawer/title tokens and the same spring). Popup's entry (its own scrim, Escape and focus trap) and ListGroup's (rows take the group's List Item Style; none set here) don't conflict. Neither this guide nor ModalSheet's, Drawer's or Popup's names the others, so an agent choosing between these bottom surfaces has only each entry's own use-when (reported). No other guidance file names ContentSheet or Content Sheet; Button's “The action leads a screen, sheet, or key step” is about Button size. Nothing hand-written here, in the guide or evidence at b4988c5, in the installed ContentSheet.tsx or in its upstream mdx uses that shape word.
